meta.title: Borderlands — wayfinding studio credentials
meta.description: Credentials deck for Borderlands, a Rotterdam wayfinding studio: point of view, three principles, three measured cases (a hospital, a bike park, a campus), clients, a client's voice and how a project runs.

slides.heading: We design signs nobody has to think about.
slides.lead: Hospitals, stations and campuses where 40 million people a year find their way.

slides.heading: A good sign answers the next question before you ask it
slides.lead: One letter, one word, one arrow per decision.
slides.imageAlt: A black-bordered hospital sign with three rows: A Outpatients right, B Radiology ahead, C Exit and Parking left

slides.heading: Three rules shape every system we draw

cards.title: One word per decision
cards.body: Never two names for one place.

slides.heading: Three zones replaced 41 department names at Westhaven
slides.lead: Visitors now reach any clinic in three decisions.

slides.heading: One naming grid cut first-week help-desk visits 47%
slides.lead: 38 buildings named by quarter and number.
slides.imageAlt: Campus map with buildings coded N1 to N3, E1 to E3, W1, W2, S1 and S2 along two crossing axes

slides.heading: Help-desk questions fell by half across 12 measured projects

slides.quote: Our front desk used to be an information booth. Now it is a front desk again.
slides.by: Marieke de Wit, facilities director, Westhaven Hospital

slides.heading: Every project runs four phases in 20 weeks
slides.notes: Stress the cardboard test: it is where clients see the system work before they pay for metal.

slides.heading: Show us where people get lost, and we will draw the way out
slides.lead: Site walks are free and take one morning.
